headline: India's inflation breaches central bank's 6% limit, bolsters case for rate hikes - AOL
summary: India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, breaching the central bank's 6% limit for the first time under the new series. The breach strengthens the case for rate hikes, per Reuters.
why: The Reserve Bank of India sets interest rates to keep inflation within its target band, so breaches shape bond yields, the rupee and equity valuations.
why_moved: Retail inflation of 6.09% in October breached the 6% central-bank limit for the first time under the new series, strengthening the case for rate hikes.
